body:
## Problem

After a #674 hold, the advice the run gives contradicts itself. At the end of the run, #674 (PR #690) tells the operator to rebuild the held bundle on a base that holds its partner. The natural next step is to re-issue the batch. That reaches the #646 pre-wave carry, which refuses the held bundle with a different message. It calls the clash "an undeclared cross-wave overlap" and says to "get issue_11's PR open with its branch on origin (re-open it, `pdca publish 11`, or re-drive issue_11), then re-issue" (on PR #690's tree: `flow.py:1050`, hint text at `flow.py:913`, `integrate.py:630`; the same wording on `main` is at `integrate.py:514`).

For a #674 hold that advice is wrong. The clash was same-wave, not cross-wave, and the PR is already open, so re-publishing changes nothing.

## Evidence (eduralph/pdca-pdca, issue_674, signed off 2026-10-14)

The reviewer re-issued the batch after a #674 hold and got the carry message above (§6 of the bundle). The brief left the carry message out of scope on purpose. It is listed in PR #690's "Known limits" and in the bundle's §10.

## Possible fix

When the carry refuses a finished bundle that the previous run held for a same-wave conflict, name the partner and give the #674 remedy (rebuild it on a base that holds the partner, or merge the partner first). Do not give the "get its PR open" hint.

## Done when

Re-issuing a batch after a #674 hold prints advice that matches the end-of-run advice and names the conflicting partner. A test pins it.

Depends on #674 / PR #690 landing. Raised by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-14.
title: flow: re-issuing after a #674 conflict hold gives the #646 carry's 'cross-wave, get the PR open' advice
